messages:
amy: Quick brain-dump: propose a lightweight 'soft-admit' in the ingress proxy. Idea: edge issues very short-lived provisional tickets so we can let low-risk requests proceed without a full RTT to central. Central ledger stays SOT; edge reconciles async. Tradeoffs: lower p99 latency vs exposure window.

devin: Okay, sketch the reconciliation and safety model. How do we prevent clients from probing many edges to game provisonals?

amy: Plan: provisional_id = opaque uuid bound to client_hash+edge_id; expire in ~2s. Edge keeps a small per-client provisional cap and a cooldown token-bucket. Edge batches reconcile calls (e.g., every 200ms or when batch > 50). Central keeps a tiny outstanding counter per client to cap cross-edge exposure.

kiran: Abuse vectors: synthetic clients spamming edges. Controls: per-edge TB, central outstanding caps, optional lightweight PoW for unknown/high-rate clients. Also central can emit a 'danger' tighten signal to edges.

sam: Reconcile API example: POST /v1/reconcile {provisional_ids:[...], window_ms:2000} -> {accepted:[...], refused:[...]}. On refuse, edge marks response degraded and triggers refund/penalty metrics.

lee: Fallback: if central unreachable, edges should default to conservative admits (e.g., 10% throughput or maintain a reserve). No opening of floodgates. Use exponential backoff for reconcile. Telemetry: provisional_issue_rate, accept_rate, reject_rate, degrade_ratio.

devin: Keep SDK tiny: Admit(ctx, clientID, hints) -> (allowed, provisionalID, reason). Opaque IDs preferred. Reconciliation must be idempotent.

amy: Rollout: prototype in staging (opt-in flag), internal beta with a few tenants, Dedicated opt-in, gradual ramp with metric gates. Action owners: amy(RFC), devin(prototype), kiran(telemetry/alerts), lee(edge TB + danger signal), sam(abuse test harness).

ops-bot: Created staging-reserve 'soft-admit-proto', quota: 8k qps across 2 nodes.

kiran: Also document UX for central-deny-after-edge-allow: degrade response gracefully, optionally retry or refund token usage. Avoid silent drops.

amy: Thanks — will draft RFC and diagrams, sync tomorrow 11am.
